title: Seventh Word Interpreting The Comparison Death Belief Patience And Reliance

questions.question: In the passage, who does the soldier stand for?
questions.answer: He stands for each human being.

questions.question: What does the lion mean in the comparison?
questions.answer: It means a person’s set time to die.

questions.question: What does the gallows mean?
questions.answer: It means death, losing things, and saying goodbye to loved ones.

questions.question: What do the two wounds stand for?
questions.answer: They stand for people being very weak and very needy.

questions.question: What are the two special helps, or talismans?
questions.answer: They are belief in Allah and belief in the Hereafter.

questions.question: How does belief in the Hereafter change the meaning of death for a believer?
questions.answer: It makes death like a ride taking the believer to Paradise.

questions.question: Why did some wise people welcome death, based on this passage?
questions.answer: Because they saw it was a way to go to mercy and happiness, not only an end.

questions.question: How does belief in Allah change the way a person sees time passing and parting from things?
questions.answer: It helps the person see Allah’s beautiful works instead of only feeling loss.

questions.question: What picture is used to show that new and better things can appear when old things change?
questions.answer: The passage uses mirrors and changing movie scenes.

questions.question: Who is being spoken to at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: The self, or nafs.

questions.question: What lesson is given about the soldier in the story?
questions.answer: The soldier is a picture of every person.

questions.question: In this comparison, what does the lion teach us to remember?
questions.answer: It teaches us to remember the time of death.

questions.question: What do the two hurts on the soldier show about people?
questions.answer: They show that people are not strong by themselves and that they need many things.

questions.question: What does the passage say the journey includes?
questions.answer: It includes life from before birth, growing up, old age, the grave, and the rising again.

questions.question: What belief helps a person with the long journey?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah and the Last Day helps with it.

questions.question: What happens to death when a person believes in the Last Day?
questions.answer: It becomes like a gentle mount that carries the believer to a beautiful place.

questions.question: According to the passage, where does that ride take the believer?
questions.answer: It takes the believer from this world to the gardens of Paradise and to Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: What does belief in Allah help a person notice in the world?
questions.answer: It helps the person notice Allah’s power, mercy, and beautiful creation.

questions.question: Is the soldier meant to be only one person from long ago, or all people?
questions.answer: He is meant to represent all people.

questions.question: What is one hard thing the two wounds tell us about human beings?
questions.answer: Human beings are weak.

questions.question: What is the other hard thing the two wounds tell us about human beings?
questions.answer: Human beings have many needs.

questions.question: Why is the journey called long in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it stretches through many stages, from early life to what comes after death.

questions.question: Which two beliefs are called the special keys or talismans?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah and belief in the Hereafter.

questions.question: Which one of those two beliefs is linked most directly to death becoming easier to face?
questions.answer: Belief in the Hereafter.

questions.question: How is death described for a believer instead of as something only scary?
questions.answer: It is described like a trained ride that carries the believer onward.

questions.question: What feeling about death did wise people have after understanding its true meaning?
questions.answer: They felt love for it and were ready for it.

questions.question: How does belief in Allah help with sadness about things changing and ending?
questions.answer: It helps a person see that Allah keeps showing new beauty and wisdom.

questions.question: What does the example of changing reflections and changing scenes help the reader understand?
questions.answer: It helps the reader understand that change can bring new beauty.

questions.question: In the story, what does the lion behind the soldier represent?
questions.answer: It represents the coming time of death.

questions.question: In the story, what does the gallows in front of the soldier represent?
questions.answer: It represents death, fading away, and being separated from loved ones.

questions.question: Why are the two wounds a good picture for people’s lives?
questions.answer: Because people are both weak and full of needs.

questions.question: What are some parts of the long journey named in the passage?
questions.answer: They include the womb, childhood, old age, the grave, and the resurrection.

questions.question: What are the two great helps given for this hard journey?
questions.answer: They are faith in Allah and faith in the Hereafter.

questions.question: What change happens to death through faith in the Hereafter?
questions.answer: It changes from something frightening into a way to reach Paradise.

questions.question: What change happens to passing time through faith in Allah?
questions.answer: It changes from only loss into a chance to see Allah’s signs and wonders.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention beautiful colors, patterns, and scenes?
questions.answer: To show that Allah keeps making fresh and lovely things.

questions.question: What does the lion remind every person about?
questions.answer: It reminds every person that death has an appointed time.

questions.question: What do the gallows remind a person about life in this world?
questions.answer: They remind a person that people and things do not stay forever.

questions.question: The wounds are not cuts to skin in the meaning of the story. What are they?
questions.answer: They are weakness and neediness.

questions.question: What does the road of exile teach about human life?
questions.answer: It teaches that life is a long trip through many stages.

questions.question: Which beliefs are the answer to the soldier’s trouble?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah and belief in the Hereafter.

questions.question: How does the passage compare death to something helpful for a believer?
questions.answer: It compares death to a ride that carries the believer onward.

questions.question: What good place is named as the destination for believers?
questions.answer: The gardens of Paradise.

questions.question: When time passes and things change, what can a believer notice because of faith in Allah?
questions.answer: The believer can notice Allah’s mercy, power, and beautiful acts.

questions.question: If old scenes pass and new scenes come, what lesson does the passage teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that change is not only loss; it can also show new beauty from Allah.

questions.question: Who is the “you” in the meaning of the soldier story?
questions.answer: It is the human being.

questions.question: What does the passage say the lion really is?
questions.answer: It is the fixed time when death comes.

questions.question: What does the passage say the gallows really is?
questions.answer: It is death and the loss and parting that happen in life.

questions.question: Name the two troubles shown by the wounds.
questions.answer: They are weakness and poverty, meaning great need.

questions.question: What does the long journey include besides life in this world?
questions.answer: It also includes before birth, the grave, and the life to come.

questions.question: What two beliefs are called talismans in this passage?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah and belief in the Hereafter.

questions.question: What does belief in the Hereafter do to the fear of death?
questions.answer: It turns death into a hopeful path to Paradise.

questions.question: Why might wise people not fear death in the same way?
questions.answer: Because they understand it leads the believer to mercy and a better home.

questions.question: What does belief in Allah help a person see when days and nights keep changing?
questions.answer: It helps the person see Allah’s ongoing creation and beauty.

questions.question: What is one clear message from the whole passage for a Muslim child?
questions.answer: Trust Allah and remember the Hereafter, because faith helps us face hard things.
